newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Spot dlr rise boosts Hungary BCE FX futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Spot dlr rise boosts Hungary BCE FX futures trade.

text.p: The Hungarian currency futures market saw increased trade on Tuesday, notably on the Budapest Commodities Exchange (BCE), as price movements adjusted to the soaring dollar/mark on the spot merket.
The BCE recorded a substantial 11.4 billion forints turnover while the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw a modest 230 million forints, made up mainly of one large deal for December marks.
"Both volume and price movements reflected the soaring dollar/mark on the spot market," one BCE dealer said.

On the BCE, the September mark, which accounted for 39,000 of the 77,102 lots traded, fell 25 fillers to 112.75 forints and the September dollar, which saw 19,000 lots traded, rose 1.20 forints to 190.40 forints.
BSE trade was dominated by one contract for the December mark worth 174 million forints.
"That particular deal was a one-off customer order rather than anything speculative," said Robert Cselovszki of WestLB Investment. "There were no real trends on the BSE today."

BSE price movements also reflected spot developments, with the mark falling for June, September and December by between 0.70 and 1.08 forints and the dollar rising for all contracts by between 0.94 and 1.46 forints.
